subject: Indemnity allocation for model output vs third-party claims — tech-witness proposal
messages:
From: Patrick Owens <patrick.owens@heliogen.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial draft: indemnity split — model outputs vs 3rd-party claims

Marcus / Kimberly —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're working through the MSA + order form and the indemnity section is the main outstanding commercial/legal point for us. Our in-house counsel flagged two areas that need clarity before we can proceed to procurement:

1) Scope trigger: whether claims alleging IP infringement by "model-generated output" are treated the same as third-party claims that arise from customer-supplied content.
2) Defense control & tech-witness: who controls litigation, and whether there should be a neutral technical witness process for disputes about whether the output came from Redwood's model or from customer input.

Attached is our redline (Redline_Draft_v2.docx) that tries to carve model-output that is purely generated by the model into a different bucket (Heliogen defends customer-provided data, Redwood defends model defects). That said, we are open to a split responsibility model if Redwood adopts reasonable technical controls and an agreed process for evidence preservation.

Can Kimberly propose a short, operational clause that lets both sides move forward? If we can get a one‑page operational playbook (who notices, who preserves KV cache, tech-witness selection method) we can take that to procurement and legal next week.

Patrick
Senior Counsel
Heliogen Systems

Attachments: Redline_Draft_v2.docx (docx)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Jun 2028 12:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Initial draft: indemnity split — model outputs vs 3rd-party claims

Patrick —

Appreciate the clear framing. Quick response while I sync internal counsel:

- We agree in principle to a split approach, but we need definitions that are operational (e.g., "Model-Generated Output" vs "Customer-Provided Content").
- We're willing to take defend-and-indemnify for third-party IP claims that result from our model behavior, but only where the customer-provided input was not the proximate cause (we'll propose a standard proximate-cause test).
- Tech-witness: good idea. Proposal: a standing roster of three mutually-acceptable technical experts; if a dispute occurs, parties jointly select one; selection process and limited scope to determine source attribution only.

I've added a short note (Marcus_notes.txt) with implementation suggestions for evidence preservation (KV caching snapshot window, minimal metadata to capture, contact for emergency preservation). Kimberly — could you draft proposed clause language and a one-page technical-witness procedure? Jordan — will you weigh in on the procurement timeline (do we need an exec credit ask to move this forward)?

--
Marcus Lin
Head of Legal Ops (on behalf of Redwood Contracts)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Marcus_notes.txt (txt)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Patrick Owens <patrick.owens@heliogen.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Jun 2028 09:30:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Initial draft: indemnity split — model outputs vs 3rd-party claims

Marcus / Patrick / Jordan —

Thanks for the framing. I put together a compact clause and an operational paragraph for the one‑page playbook; attaching the snippet (KM_indemnity_snippet.docx). High-level points:

- Definitions: "Model-Generated Output" = content generated by Redwood models where the content is not a verbatim reproduction or direct transformation of Customer-Provided Content. "Customer-Provided Content" = data, prompts, documents or code provided to Redwood by the Customer.
- Liability split: Redwood will indemnify and defend claims alleging third-party IP infringement to the extent they arise from Model-Generated Output. Customer will indemnify claims resulting from Customer-Provided Content. For mixed claims we propose a proportional allocation based on proximate cause tied to factual record.
- Defense control: default to the indemnifying party, but opposing party has right to independent counsel at its own cost for conflict situations.
- Tech-witness & evidence preservation: 48-hour hold on ephemeral caches after notice; party seeking preservation pays for forensics unless the indemnifying party concedes. Neutral tech-witness appointment: both parties supply a roster of three candidates; select by mutual agreement or, failing that within five business days, by the Chair of the AAA (or similar agreed method).

Open items for Redwood to consider: cap/aggregate limits, insurance waterfall language, and whether we want to require an initial meet-and-confer before litigation defense control formally transfers.

Patrick — does the tech-witness roster approach work for you? If yes, I'll draft counter-redline to your Redline_Draft_v2 and include the one-page procedure.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: KM_indemnity_snippet.docx (docx)

From: Patrick Owens <patrick.owens@heliogen.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Ellen Shaw <ellen.shaw@stellarlegal.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Jun 2028 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial draft: indemnity split — model outputs vs 3rd-party claims

Kimberly / Marcus —

Thanks — the snippet looks like real progress. A few clarifying points from our side (and our procurement counsel):

- We can accept the roster idea for a tech-witness. Two asks: (a) the roster should include at least one expert with ML infra experience (KV cache, beam search, quantization), and (b) selection fallback should be a named neutral (we propose the Computer Science department at State University X or AAA if agreeable).
- We remain concerned about the initial preservation costs. Proposal: fines for failure to preserve evidence only where a party is shown to have acted in bad faith; otherwise the preservation burden is shared 50/50.
- Insurance & cap: we prefer a relatively low cap on Redwood's indemnity for model output while requesting a covenant to maintain a minimum cyber/tech E&O tower during the term.

I've attached our annotated redline (Heliogen_redline.pdf) showing the changes we'd accept and remaining asks. If Redwood can produce a counter-redline that (1) accepts the roster method, (2) proposes a compromise on preservation costs, and (3) includes a modest cap tied to insurance levels, procurement can sign off next week.

Would appreciate a quick 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the remaining points.

Best,
Patrick Owens
Senior Counsel
Heliogen Systems

- Kimberly: please produce a counter-redline that: (a) integrates the roster + named fallback neutral; (b) includes the 48-hour KV cache preservation window but pins cost-shifting mechanics to a meet-and-confer with a bad-faith threshold (Patrick's shared-cost suggestion is reasonable); and (c) proposes a cap formula: lesser of $5M or 2x annual contract value, with carveouts for willful misconduct.
